claims.claim: Reviewers report that the hacking minigame features hidden codes or mechanics that are explained once but later change without warning or clear feedback.

citations.review_text: I loved this game, I want to complete it. I want to do all the things. But I won't. You explain the hidden codes for the hacking mini-game once, then midway through the game suddenly have the codes be wrong and never once explain that can happen or even give a way to be able to spot it before it screws us. this is an interactive movie, don't put hidden mechanics in the game with such piss poor execution and expect people to be happy. I know this stupid mechanic has been reported as a bug over and over and over, and instead of going in and patching a text box in that explains it, you just close the tickets and leave us angry.

Okay obviously fantastic story, the fact that more people choose invisigal is weird considering spoiler alert she punches you, abandons the team, tries to sabotage the team, blows you up, steals your cool power thing, is a huge perv but i guess the fact the game tells me 60% of you are weird is pretty cool and only 13% of you left her tied up in episdode 8 i bet you all felt like idiots when Shroud said she was a mole (which was super obvious but kinda weird like she is a terrible mole she helps you fight him and almost kills him with a bomb yet hes like ye thats my best agent there, the entirity of Invisigals story just felt really stupid to me like they kept changing her halfway through the game one minute shes warning a guy your about to tase who could have easily turned around quicker and murdered Robert next minute shes saving your life damn maybe the story changes if you pick the option to bone the creepy chick who has s*x dreams about you and makes a bit more sense with her character). Now the game as a game actually kinda sucks a lot of the choices are just super obvious and effect the game in really obvious generic ways like you pick Moist Bat to kick off the team and guess what your fight him at the end, shocker, and the hacking minigame is the absolute most dull thing ever it is either super easy or the most hard thing ever no in between one of them you literally have to just guess a combination code with no hints, it is a minor complaint but the fact that that is the only active gameplay with a bit of action and it sucks is a bit lame. The fact that they even bothered putting a QTE system in the game too for like 3 scenes or something is strange i wouldnt have mi ded a few more click amd drag the mouse to put mask on or whatever. i would say 8/10 solid story reasonably engrossing not as much content as a telltale game probably about 3 or 4 hours of like cutscene story stuff and 3 or 4 hours of dispathching heroes and looking at stats in the credits depen…

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: The game runs exceptionally well on modest hardware and offers a mode to bypass quick-time events.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as running very well on low-end hardware and the Steam Deck without performance issues.

citations.review_text:
I loved this game. These kind of Telltale-esque episodic adventures aren't usually my bag, but this game was awesome. Choices felt like they mattered, the writing was clever, the characters were likeable, and the voice acting was phenomenal. 

The overarching story and the character of Robert really resonated with me, and I wish I could play through blind again. I found myself fully invested in each of my runs. The magic [b] does [/b] fade a little in subsequent playthroughs, as is usually the case with these kind of games, but not enough to make them any less enjoyable.

Approx 31 or so hours all in. This makes up 2 proper playthroughs and a 'speedrun' to mop up missed achievements. I even had a blast mopping those up, particularly when I was forced to play a little differently than I otherwise would have, except perhaps the [spoiler] "We can just be friends" [/spoiler] achievement 💔.

I played this through on the SteamDeck and it played flawlessly. No complaints with performance. I would wholeheartedly recommend finishing and 100% completing Dispatch.

Dispatch is a love letter to the superhero genre, with a fresh take on gamemaking with it's Dispatching system.

The characters make this game such an endearing and well made story. Highly recommend.  This game can run decently on lowend computers too, which is a positive for my potato of a laptop.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention an included story mode that allows players to bypass the quick-time event (QTE) sections.

citations.review_text:
I heard of this around the time when it was announced, but I never got the chance to really play it. More specifically, I didn't really bother to give it a chance and figured I would just watch it at some point. Eventually it went on sale, so I picked it up and I can confidently say that I would have absolutely paid the original price and probably even a bit more had it been more expensive.

This is an incredible experience with some stellar voice acting, captivating art style, and writing that is actually pretty great (save for a few moments that I won't mention because of spoilers, but the rest of the game is so great that it makes up for them in droves).


Pros:

- Visually captivating. The fights, the expressions on the characters' faces, the romance, the heartbreak. The choices on some of the angles are top tier.
- A long list of different outcomes that require multiple playthroughs, so plenty of fun to be had
- Doing multiple playthroughs does not feel overly repetitive, even if you make similar choices
- I actually laughed out loud to a lot of the lines and their deliveries. Other times it was really easy to feel emotional and empathize with the characters. Really impressive voice acting and more so chemistry between the VA's. It definitely seemed like everybody working on this wanted to be there.
- Ability to disable QTEs
- Copy save mechanic. For multiple runs without having to replay through 4 episodes that are about an hour each just to get a certain achievement or outcome.
- It has this charm to it where you'll see a picture or frame of the game and say "yeah, that's 'Dispatch'". It just feels entirely original to me. 
- The actual dispatching is extremely satisfying. This is one of the only games where you as the player clock into work and it's actually enjoyable and engaging. By the time the game ends you don't even fully realize that you sat at a computer and sent heroes out to answer calls without ever actually seeing a lick of the action (other than…

Excellent story telling and art, the voice acting is very polished, if you havnt played it yet i urge you to give it a try.  Replay value is high due to experiencing the other characters story, also has a story mode where you dont have to do the qte parts which i found really nice.  Definately reccomend!

single_points.text: One reviewer notes that you cannot skip through text or cutscenes, which can become tedious when watching repeat scenes in a choices-matter game.

citation.review_text:
Love this game - funny, great story, great mini games, great production quality. Super fun to play. 

Only negative is you can't skip through text or cutscenes which can get a bit tedious in a choices matter game watching repeat scenes. Minor issue with all the positives though.

single_points.text: One reviewer reports having to download 12 gigabytes of content.

citation.review_text: Why do I have to download 12 gigabytes of content if I'm not allowed to use it without paying for it first. You should be ashamed of yourselves, AdHoc. This game was already sitting idle in my library cause I've already played through it as many times as I care to, but this warrants an uninstall.
